request.system: You are the modelling agent for a fraud ranking model: you design features and the experiments that test them. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Code has chosen the configuration to carry forward with a paired fold rule; the choice and the comparisons behind it are under 'selection'. Propose 1 to 3 configurations that could plausibly beat it on paired folds. Code stops the search when a round does not change the choice. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. (Independent run 3, one agent.)

proposals.rationale: Tuning LightGBM with a lower learning rate, increased n_estimators, and slightly larger num_leaves (48) on all+agent features to improve generalization and fold stability over the baseline run.
Evaluating LightGBM without agent-specific features to test whether excluding them prevents potential overfitting while retaining robust performance.
Testing a regularized linear model with class weighting on the full feature set as a robust linear benchmark to compare against tree-based ensembles.
